chunks: And from him (narrated) from him, from Fadalah, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Salim al-Ashall, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dog that holds onto your game after it has eaten from it, so he said: 'There is no harm in it; it merely ate, and it is permissible for you.'
ai.seo_question: Is game caught by a dog halal if the dog eats part of it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a hunting dog's consumption of the prey does not invalidate its permissibility, distinguishing between mere eating and the act of *akl* (devouring) which might render it *makruh* or *haram* depending on the school of thought. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the dog's saliva or partial consumption does not impart impurity (*najasah*) to the meat, provided the dog was trained and the owner invoked Allah's name. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions of *dhikr* and the physical state of the hunting animal in Shia jurisprudence.
